messages:
maria: quick flag - noticing a subtle but repeatable quality regression for long-context Llama v2 after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. some summaries hallucinate on lines >100
ben: which selector change? perf impact? :thinking_face:
maria: selector now prefers tiled-attn for heads>=16 on llm-llama-13b to boost throughput. perf +12% throughput, p95 slightly down. quality drop on long-context subset.
sam: can you paste a failing prompt and a profiling snippet? let's check kv-cache behavior and rope params.
maria: failing prompt (sanitized):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the meeting notes from lines 120-340"
Expected: "Key outcomes: ..."
Got: "I can’t access that document"
```
profile excerpt: 
```
kernel: tiled-attn selected
kv-cache hit rate: 0.96 -> 0.42 (long seq)
rope_scale_factor: 1.15
latency p95: 180ms -> 170ms
quality metric (bert-score-ish): drop -3.1
```
cheng: big red flag is kv-cache hit drop. tiled path may be indexing past_kv differently (tiling offsets). small off-by-one in the offset math would desync RoPE positions.
ben: agreed. tiled partitioning can change how we compute absolute positions when reusing past_kv. could also be clamp behavior on tiled kernels.
maria: reproduced locally by forcing tiled-attn path; failure repro ~92% on long-context eval.
sam: quick mitigations: 1) soft revert selector for Llama long-context routes; 2) instrument nvprof and dump past_kv indices for a failing step; 3) run quant variants (q4_0/q5_0) to check interplay.
ben: +1 to canary revert. add nvprof traces and side-by-side kv dumps (raw indices). I'll collect CUDA kernels and offsets.
cheng: I'll write a fast unit that diffs past_kv shapes & indices across kernels for identical inputs. should catch this in CI.
maria: plan: canary revert to small-batch kernel on dedicated, run full eval and perf benchmark. if revert fixes quality we can patch tiled-attn. window ~2h.
deploy-bot: deploy request by maria: revert-selector -> staging-dedicated (id: dply-204)
sam: also sweep quant toggles. earlier we saw q4_0 trigger sensitivity when rope_scale != 1. run both quant and non-quant baseline.
ben: if revert works and perf delta ok, we can keep revert and iterate on tiled fix (investigate tiling offsets and RoPE application).
maria: will update with canary results. starting canary now. :rocket:
cheng: noted. I'll land the unit test PR and attach to smoke checks.
ben: after dumps, run a diff of positional embeddings applied to last tokens across kernels. that should reveal any shift.
maria: quick note: telemetry shows error spikes at ~10:42 UTC across several customer routes using long contexts. might correlate with canary of selector yesterday.
sam: good catch. add that to the incident timeline.
deploy-bot: canary deployed (id: dply-204) by maria -> staging-dedicated.
maria: canary passed perf check but eval quality still failing. rolling back now to stable selector on dedicated.
ben: when you rollback, keep trace capture on the failing requests so we can compare.
maria: rollback initiated. will attach trace bundle in follow-up.
cheng: created PR: attn-kernel-pastkv-consistency-test. tiny diff, adds small input microtests.
sam: after we have kv index dumps and nvprof, we should run a targeted small-batch experiment where we force different rope_scale values to see sensitivity.
maria: agree. next steps summary: 1) collect kernel nvprof + raw past_kv indices (ben) 2) run quant sweep q4_0/q5_0 + baseline (sam) 3) land consistency unit (cheng) 4) attempt tiled-attn with corrected offset math in a follow-up canary (maria). aim: ship fix or rollback permanent within 48h.
ben: I'll also add a short runtime flag: runtime.flag.attn_compat to quickly toggle compatibility behavior per-model.
maria: thanks. will follow up with trace bundle and smoke results. :white_check_mark:
